units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 26. A banking support clause shall be included in the contract in the cases established under Article 35 of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 26 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 27. The contract must state the time limits for the contracting authority to return money deposited by the supplier (contractor, service provider) as contract performance security, if that form of security is used, including the relevant portion where security is reduced under parts 7, 7.1 and 7.2 of Article 96 of this Federal Law. The return period must not exceed thirty days after performance of the supplier’s contractual obligations, or fifteen days where the contracting authority has imposed the restriction provided for by part 3 of Article 30 of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 27 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 28. When a contract for forest guarding, protection or reproduction works is concluded under Article 19 of the Forest Code of the Russian Federation, it shall include an additional term on the sale of forest stands for timber harvesting.
units.label: Part 28 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 29. The Government of the Russian Federation may determine:
units.label: Part 29 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 1) the procedure for determining the minimum period for a supplier (contractor, service provider) to perform a contract;
units.label: Point 1 Part 29 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 2) requirements for forming lots in procurement of particular types of goods, works or services.
units.label: Point 2 Part 29 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 29.1. When procuring works or services specified in points 3–5 of part 4 of Article 48 of this Federal Law, the contract may require the contractor to perform the works or the service provider to provide the services itself, without engaging other persons to perform contractual obligations.
units.label: Part 29.1 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 34. Contract
units.text: 30. Where the contracting authority requires contract performance security under part 1 of Article 96 of this Federal Law, the contract shall oblige the supplier (contractor, service provider), if the bank that issued an independent guarantee as security has its banking licence revoked under legislation of the Russian Federation, to provide replacement security within one month after due notice from the contracting authority. The amount may be reduced in the manner and cases provided for by parts 7, 7.1, 7.2 and 7.3 of Article 96 of this Federal Law. For each day of delay, a penalty shall accrue in the amount determined under the procedure established pursuant to part 7 of this Article.
units.label: Part 30 Art. 34

units.locator: Article 35. Banking support for contracts
units.text: Article 35. Banking support for contracts
units.label: Art. 35

units.locator: Article 35. Banking support for contracts
units.text: 1. The Government of the Russian Federation shall establish the procedure for banking support of contracts, including requirements for banks and their selection, terms of agreements concluded with the bank, and requirements for the content of reports prepared by banks.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 35

units.locator: Article 35. Banking support for contracts
units.text: 2. The Government of the Russian Federation, the highest executive body of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation and the local administration shall determine cases requiring banking support for contracts for goods, works or services to meet federal needs, the constituent entity’s needs and municipal needs, respectively, through regulatory legal acts of the Government, regulatory legal acts of that highest executive body, or municipal legal acts. The Government of the Russian Federation may establish a minimum initial (maximum) contract price or price of a contract with a sole supplier (contractor, service provider) to be taken into account when determining under this part the cases requiring banking support for contracts meeting a constituent entity’s or municipal needs.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 35

units.locator: Article 35. Banking support for contracts
units.text: 3. Payments during performance of a contract receiving banking support shall be reflected in accounts opened at that bank.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 35

units.locator: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.text: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.label: Art. 36

units.locator: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.text: 1. The contracting authority may cancel procurement subject to this Article. After the time limits set by this Article have expired and before contract conclusion, it may cancel procurement only in the event of force majeure.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 36

units.locator: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.text: 2. In electronic procedures and closed electronic procedures:
units.label: Part 2 Art. 36

units.locator: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.text: 1) no later than one working day before the application deadline, the contracting authority shall generate a cancellation notice through the unified information system, sign it with the enhanced electronic signature of a person authorized to act on its behalf, and publish it in that system. Procurement shall be deemed cancelled upon that publication. For closed electronic procedures, the notice shall not be published on the official website;
units.label: Point 1 Part 2 Art. 36

units.locator: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.text: 2) no later than one hour after the cancellation notice is published in the unified information system under point 1 of this part, the electronic platform operator or specialized electronic platform operator shall return submitted applications to participants and notify them of publication of the cancellation notice.
units.label: Point 2 Part 2 Art. 36

units.locator: Article 36. Cancellation of procurement
units.text: 3. In a closed tender or closed auction, the contracting authority shall, no later than five days before the application deadline, return submitted applications and notify all invited participants that procurement is cancelled. Procurement shall be deemed cancelled when the notification is sent.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 36

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.label: Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 1. Where the initial (maximum) contract price in a tender or auction exceeds fifteen million rubles and the participant with whom the contract is to be concluded offers a price at least twenty-five percent below that initial price, or a total of unit prices of goods, works or services at least twenty-five percent below the initial total, the contract may be concluded only after that participant provides performance security, if required under Article 96 of this Federal Law, equal to one and a half times the amount specified in the procurement notice and documentation, where such documentation is required. It must be no less than ten percent of the initial (maximum) contract price or of the concluded contract price where supplier (contractor, service provider) selection was conducted under point 1 of part 1 of Article 30 of this Federal Law, and no less than the advance payment, if one is provided for.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 2. Where the initial (maximum) contract price in a tender or auction is fifteen million rubles or less and the participant with whom the contract is to be concluded offers a price at least twenty-five percent below that initial price, or a total of unit prices of goods, works or services at least twenty-five percent below the initial total, the contract may be concluded only after that participant provides performance security, if required under Article 96 of this Federal Law, in the amount specified in part 1 of this Article; or provides information confirming its good faith under part 3 of this Article and simultaneously provides security in the amount stated in the procurement notice, invitation and documentation, where such documentation is required.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 3. Information confirming a participant’s good faith means information in the register of contracts concluded by contracting authorities confirming that the participant, taking account of legal succession, performed three contracts during the three years before applying without contractual penalties (fines or late-performance penalties). At least one of those contracts must have a price no less than twenty percent of the initial (maximum) contract price stated in the procurement notice, invitation and documentation, where such documentation is required.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 4. In a closed tender, the participant shall include the information provided for by part 3 of this Article in its application. The procurement commission shall reject the application if that information is found unreliable. The rejection and its reasons shall be recorded in the supplier (contractor, service provider) selection record and communicated to the applicant no later than the working day after the record is signed. If, in the case provided for by part 2 of this Article, the participant does not include information confirming good faith under part 3 of this Article, the contract shall be concluded after it provides performance security, if required under Article 96 of this Federal Law, equal to one and a half times the amount stated in the procurement notice, invitation and documentation, where such documentation is required.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 5. In an electronic tender or an auction, the participant shall provide the information specified in part 3 of this Article when sending the signed draft contract to the contracting authority. If the winner fails to do so, or the contracting authority finds that information unreliable, no contract shall be concluded with it and it shall be deemed to have evaded conclusion under this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 6. The participant with whom the contract is to be concluded shall provide the security specified in parts 1 and 2 of this Article before conclusion, if security is required under Article 96 of this Federal Law. A participant that fails to do so shall be deemed to have evaded conclusion. That evasion shall be recorded in a document published in the unified information system and communicated to all participants no later than the working day after it is signed.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 7. In tenders for research, experimental design or technological work or consulting services, the contracting authority may establish different application evaluation criterion weights in the procurement notice, invitation and documentation, where required, depending on whether the offered contract price is:
units.label: Part 7 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 1) less than twenty-five percent below the initial (maximum) contract price;
units.label: Point 1 Part 7 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 2) twenty-five percent or more below the initial (maximum) contract price.
units.label: Point 2 Part 7 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 8. In the cases provided for by point 2 of part 7 of this Article, the contract price criterion shall have a weight of ten percent of the combined weights of all application evaluation criteria.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 9. In a tender or auction for goods necessary for citizens’ normal subsistence, a participant offering a contract price or total of unit prices at least twenty-five percent below the respective initial price or total must, in addition to meeting this Article’s requirements, justify the offered price or total to the contracting authority. The justification may include a manufacturer’s guarantee letter stating the price and quantity of goods to be supplied, unless the quantity cannot be determined; documents confirming that the participant has the goods; and other documents and calculations confirming its ability to supply at the offered price or total.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 10. The justification specified in part 9 of this Article shall be submitted:
units.label: Part 10 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 1) by a participant offering a contract price or total of unit prices at least twenty-five percent below the respective initial price or total, as part of its closed tender application. If the participant fails to do so or the procurement commission finds the offered price or total unjustified, the application shall be rejected. The commission’s decision shall be recorded in the record of examination and evaluation of tender applications or examination of the sole application;
units.label: Point 1 Part 10 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 2) by the participant with whom the contract is to be concluded, when sending the signed draft contract in an electronic tender or auction. Failure to do so shall be treated as evasion of contract conclusion. If the procurement commission finds the offered contract price or total of unit prices unjustified, no contract shall be concluded with that participant; the right to conclude shall pass to a participant offering the same price or total as the winner or the next best contract price terms after the winner. The commission’s decision shall be recorded in a document published in the unified information system and communicated to all participants no later than the working day after it is signed.
units.label: Point 2 Part 10 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 11. Where the tender or auction winner is deemed to have evaded contract conclusion, this Article shall apply in full to the participant with whom the contract is concluded under this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 12. This Article shall not apply where, in procurement of medicines included in the list of vital and essential medicines approved by the Government of the Russian Federation, the participant with whom the contract is to be concluded offers prices for all procured medicines reduced by no more than twenty-five percent relative to their maximum ex-factory prices registered under legislation on the circulation of medicines.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 37. Anti-dumping measures in tenders and auctions
units.text: 13. Advance payments are prohibited in performance of a contract concluded with a participant specified in part 1 or 2 of this Article.
units.label: Part 13 Art. 37

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.label: Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 1. Contracting authorities whose aggregate annual procurement volume exceeds one hundred million rubles shall create contract services; a separate structural unit need not be established.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 2. Where a contracting authority’s aggregate annual procurement volume does not exceed one hundred million rubles and it has no contract service, it shall appoint an official responsible for one or more procurements, including performance of each contract (hereinafter, the contract manager).
units.label: Part 2 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 3. A contract service shall operate under rules (regulations) developed and approved on the basis of model rules (regulations) approved by the federal executive body regulating the contractual procurement system.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 4. The contract service and contract manager shall exercise the following functions and powers:
units.label: Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 1) Repealed from 1 October 2019. — Federal Law of 01.05.2019 No. 71-FZ;
units.label: Point 1 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 2) develop the procurement schedule, prepare amendments to it, and post the schedule and its amendments in the unified information system;
units.label: Point 2 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 3) prepare and post procurement notices, procurement documentation (where this Federal Law provides for procurement documentation) and draft contracts in the unified information system, and prepare and send invitations;
units.label: Point 3 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 4) ensure that procurement is carried out, including the conclusion of contracts;
units.label: Point 4 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 5) participate in proceedings concerning challenges to the results of supplier (contractor, service provider) selection and prepare materials for claims and litigation work;
units.label: Point 5 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 6) where necessary, arrange consultations with suppliers (contractors, service providers) at the procurement planning stage and participate in them to ascertain the competitive environment in the relevant markets for goods, works and services and identify the best technologies and other solutions to meet State and municipal needs;
units.label: Point 6 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 7) exercise other powers provided for by this Federal Law.
units.label: Point 7 Part 4 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 5. Where procurement is centralized under Article 26(1) of this Federal Law, the contract service and the contract manager exercise the powers provided for by this Federal Law that have not been transferred to the relevant authorized body or authorized institution exercising powers to select suppliers (contractors, service providers). The contract service and the contract manager are liable within the scope of the powers they exercise.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 6. Employees of the contract service and the contract manager must have higher education or additional professional education in procurement.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 38. Contracting authority officials, contract service and contract manager
units.text: 7. In conducting procurement, the head of the contracting authority, the head and employees of the contract service and the contract manager must take measures to prevent and resolve conflicts of interest in accordance with Federal Law No. 273-FZ of 25 December 2008 “On Combating Corruption”, including in the light of information provided to the contracting authority under Article 34(23) of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 38

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.label: Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 1. To select suppliers (contractors, service providers), except when procuring from a sole supplier (contractor, service provider), the contracting authority shall establish a procurement commission (hereinafter in this Article, the commission).
units.label: Part 1 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 2. The contracting authority shall decide to establish the commission before procurement begins. The decision shall determine the composition and operating procedure of the commission and appoint its chair.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 2.1. The specific rules for establishing a commission when procuring specialized depositary services and fiduciary management of pension savings are laid down in Article 19 of Federal Law No. 111-FZ of 24 July 2002 “On Investing Funds to Finance the Funded Component of Labour Pensions in the Russian Federation”.
units.label: Part 2.1 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 3. The commission must have at least three members.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 4. Where tenders are held to conclude contracts for the creation of literary or artistic works or performances (as results of intellectual activity), or for financing the distribution or screening of national films, the commissions must include creative professionals in the relevant field of literature or art. Such persons must constitute at least fifty per cent of the total membership of the commission.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 5. The contracting authority shall include in the commission predominantly persons who have undergone professional retraining or advanced training in procurement, as well as persons with specialist knowledge relating to the subject matter of the procurement.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 6. The following may not be members of the commission:
units.label: Part 6 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 1) individuals engaged as experts to conduct an expert appraisal of the procurement notice, procurement documentation (where this Federal Law provides for procurement documentation), or applications to participate in a tender;
units.label: Point 1 Part 6 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 2) individuals with a personal interest in the outcome of supplier (contractor, service provider) selection, including individuals who have submitted applications to participate in supplier (contractor, service provider) selection, or are in an employment relationship with organizations or individuals that have submitted such applications, or are managers of organizations that have submitted applications to participate in supplier (contractor, service provider) selection. “Personal interest” has the meaning given in Federal Law No. 273-FZ of 25 December 2008 “On Combating Corruption”;
units.label: Point 2 Part 6 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 3) individuals who are members (shareholders) of organizations that have submitted applications to participate in procurement, members of their governing bodies, or creditors of procurement participants;
units.label: Point 3 Part 6 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 4) officials of the oversight bodies specified in Article 99(1) of this Federal Law who directly exercise procurement oversight.
units.label: Point 4 Part 6 Art. 39

units.locator: Article 39. Procurement commission
units.text: 7. A commission member may be replaced only by decision of the contracting authority that decided to establish the commission. A commission member must immediately notify that contracting authority of circumstances specified in paragraph 6 of this Article. If the commission is found to include individuals specified in paragraph 6 of this Article, the contracting authority that decided to establish the commission must immediately replace them with other individuals who meet the requirements of paragraph 6 of this Article.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 39
